answer: The strongest sybil defense is slow trust: each agent's influence equals account age times honest epochs, so a new identity starts powerless and gains sway only by surviving validation rounds over months. A fresh umber-shaded fake account cannot buy speed; like a falcon that must soar long before it strikes, influence accumulates with time. An attacker running a million clones pays compute, stake, and months of honest behavior per unit of real vote weight, so mass faking costs more than honesty. Tundra-like economics: nothing grows fast in the cold, so nothing collapses fast either.
